known_uncertainty.summary: Review by a qualified federal criminal sentencing, appellate-waiver, allocution, Guidelines, and appellate-timing practitioner remains pending; no independent review is recorded and no level-3 or gold claim is made.

Automated schema, citation, deadline, digest, render, sealed-record, and replay checks do not establish the legal accuracy, completeness, currency, or practical realism of the authored waiver, role-adjustment, allocution, Rule 4(b), or confidentiality analysis.

Record tags, stable-anchor mappings, operation bindings, and semantic classifications are authored for exact identified documents and do not generalize to novel filings, altered bytes, or unreviewed procedural circumstances.

Waiver validity, waiver scope, the express complete-denial carve-out, and the allocution remedy are authored conclusions tied to the exact plea clause, personal Rule 11 colloquy, sentencing sequence, and preserved mitigation. The system does not infer those conclusions from arbitrary plea or hearing text.

The role issue assumes exactly five criminally responsible participants and asks only whether Serrano managed or supervised another person. The actual appeal dismisses that target under the waiver without deciding the enhancement merits, and full resentencing may recalculate the Guidelines; the system does not infer participant status or role from arbitrary offense descriptions.

The isolated Rule 4(b) outcome depends on an exact day-15 district-clerk filing, no Rule 4(c) deposit, no Rule 4(b)(3) event, no clerk inaccessibility, a prompt limited remand, express disclaimer of extension, findings of neither excusable neglect nor good cause, and prompt government invocation. It is not a general timeliness or forfeiture oracle.

The August 19 core may analyze Hunter and Melvin, but source documents use only authority issued by their own dates: no pre-June 18 source cites Hunter, no pre-July 27 source cites Melvin, and the counterfactual branch cites neither. Evidence closure does not project later authority backward into earlier filings.

The record models eight public/sealed disclosure pairs through ninety-five bijective page mappings, public-default projection, exact-document session grants, revocation, and deferred per-open CAS verification. Those synthetic controls neither establish the legal propriety of sealing elsewhere nor represent access to PACER, CM/ECF, Probation, or a real presentence report.

PA156–PA196 are never-filed counterfactual branch artifacts on a distinct synthetic docket. Actual-history operations, the actual disposition, and actual-record argument questions must exclude those pages even though the complete training record resolves their anchors.

The committed workflow and two canonical traces intentionally preserve exactly two source-faithful terminal executions: actual ordinary mandate and the never-filed day-15 counterfactual ordinary mandate. Their union covers all seventy-nine workflow operations; no cross-branch or unsupported third endpoint is represented.

A custom originating-court role separates district operations from appellate operations, but the Fourth Circuit exercise clerk and fictional panel share the generic court role. Role authorization therefore cannot distinguish clerk from panel identity beyond exact authored commands, document bindings, and trace evidence.

All parties, people, offices, addresses, dockets, identifiers, facts, and events are fictional. Fraud descriptions are intentionally abstract and non-actionable; repository checks cannot establish external authenticity or authorize use as operational guidance.

The Slate, Alder, and March profiles and oral-argument behavior are fictional or composite training constructs; differentiation does not model a real judge or predict actual advocacy, questioning, or outcomes.

The PDFs are generated training artifacts. Source-to-PDF checks, the accepted render inventory, and pinned hashes document repository provenance but cannot establish external authenticity, future cross-render byte determinism, or complete accessibility and typography quality.
